title: Sunjiawan coal mine explosion
description: A gas explosion at the state-owned Sunjiawan coal mine in Fuxin, Liaoning Province, killed 214 miners and injured 30. The blast occurred about 240 metres underground while 574 miners were working the shaft, making it China's deadliest mining disaster in 15 years.

title: Winnenden School Shooting
description: On March 11, 2009, 17-year-old former student Tim Kretschmer opened fire at the Albertville-Realschule secondary school in Winnenden, Germany, killing 9 students and 3 teachers. After fleeing, he killed a passerby and two more people at a car dealership in nearby Wendlingen before being shot dead, for a total of 16 dead including the gunman. It was Germany's deadliest school shooting since the 2002 Erfurt massacre.

title: Wenchuan earthquake (Sichuan earthquake)
description: A magnitude 7.9 (Mw, USGS) / 8.0 (Ms, CEA) earthquake struck Wenchuan County in Sichuan Province at 14:28 local time on 12 May 2008, collapsing schools, factories, and villages across mountainous western Sichuan and damaging areas over 500,000 square kilometers. China's State Council Information Office confirmed 69,227 dead, 17,923 missing, and about 374,000 injured, for a combined total of roughly 87,000 dead or missing; over 15 million people were evacuated and 5 million left homeless. It was China's most destructive earthquake since 1949.

title: Indian embassy bombing in Kabul
description: A suicide car bomber rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into the gates of the Indian embassy in Kabul on the morning of 7 July 2008, killing 58 people and wounding about 140, most of them Afghan civilians queuing for visas. Among the dead were four Indian embassy staff, including the defence attaché and press counsellor, six Afghan police officers, and reportedly eight schoolchildren. The attack, blamed on elements of the Afghan Taliban and Pakistan-based militant networks, was one of the deadliest in Kabul during the war.

title: London bombings (7/7)
description: Four coordinated suicide bombings struck three London Underground trains and a double-decker bus at Tavistock Square during the morning rush hour, killing 52 commuters and injuring more than 770. It was the deadliest terrorist attack on British soil since the 1988 Lockerbie bombing.

title: Ethiopia floods (Dire Dawa and Omo Valley)
description: Unusually intense seasonal rains in August 2006 caused two major flood disasters in Ethiopia: a flash flood of the Dechatu River in the city of Dire Dawa on August 6 killed 256 people with about 250 missing, and flooding of the Omo River in the remote South Omo Valley on August 13 killed 364 people and submerged five villages. Combined flood deaths across the country in 2006 reached about 640, with roughly 118,000 people affected and tens of thousands displaced.
sources: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)

title: Bali bombings
description: Three suicide bombers attacked restaurants in Kuta Square and on Jimbaran beach in Bali, Indonesia, killing 20 victims and wounding more than 100. The attacks, attributed to Jemaah Islamiyah, killed a total of 23 people including the three bombers.

title: Al-Askari shrine bombing triggers sectarian violence
description: Bombers dressed as security personnel detonated explosives inside the al-Askari shrine in Samarra on February 22, 2006, destroying the golden dome of one of Shia Islam's holiest sites. The blast itself killed no one, but it triggered waves of retaliatory sectarian killings across Iraq, with more than 1,000 people dead within days and hundreds of mosques attacked; leaked U.S. military documents later indicated the death toll exceeded 3,000, and the bombing is widely regarded as having ignited Iraq's civil war.

title: Iraq sectarian civil war (deadliest year of the conflict)
description: Sectarian violence between Shia and Sunni communities escalated sharply after the February 22 bombing of the al-Askari shrine, plunging Iraq into civil war conditions characterized by car bombings, executions, death squads and forced displacement. The Iraq Body Count project recorded about 29,000 violent civilian deaths in 2006, making it the deadliest year of the war since 2003, with the United Nations reporting similar monthly tolls; more than 400,000 people were displaced within Iraq during the year.
sources: United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq (UNAMI)

title: Zarand earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck near Zarand in Kerman Province, Iran, levelling several mud-brick mountain villages and killing 612 people. An estimated 80,000 people were affected and more than 900 were injured.

title: Jaipur bombings
description: Eight synchronized bombs exploded within about 15 minutes across the crowded Walled City markets of Jaipur, Rajasthan, on the evening of 13 May 2008, including near the Hawa Mahal landmark, killing 63 people and wounding more than 200. The devices included ammonium-nitrate and RDX bombs hidden on bicycles, and a previously unknown group, the Indian Mujahideen, claimed responsibility; Bangladesh-based militants were also suspected. Four men were later convicted over the attacks, though all were acquitted by the Rajasthan High Court in 2023.

title: Typhoon Morakot
description: Typhoon Morakot, the deadliest typhoon to hit Taiwan in about 50 years, made landfall on August 7-8, 2009, dumping record rainfall of up to 3 meters in the southern mountains. A massive mudslide buried the village of Xiaolin in Kaohsiung County, killing an estimated 400-500 residents. More than 670 people were confirmed dead in Taiwan, with additional deaths in China and the northern Philippines, for a regional total of roughly 700-800 lives lost.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

title: Azizabad airstrike
description: US-led coalition forces called in air strikes, including from an AC-130 gunship, on the village of Azizabad in Shindand district, Herat Province, on 22 August 2008, during an operation against a suspected Taliban commander. The Afghan government and the UN (UNAMA) said about 90 civilians were killed, including 60 children and 15 women, based on witness accounts and video evidence; the US military initially denied civilian deaths before a second inquiry acknowledged 33 civilians killed. The incident, which President Hamid Karzai condemned, became a flashpoint over civilian casualties and led Afghanistan to pay compensation to victims' families.

title: Greek forest fires
description: Widespread forest fires in Greece, most severely in the Peloponnese, burned from late August 2007 and killed 85 people across the country. Flames raced through villages, and many victims were trapped in their homes or while fleeing by car.

title: Pétion-Ville school collapse (Collège La Promesse Évangélique)
description: The three-story Collège La Promesse Évangélique school collapsed around 10:00 a.m. on 7 November 2008 while classes were in session in the Nerette neighbourhood of Pétion-Ville, a suburb of Port-au-Prince, burying hundreds of the roughly 500-700 students and teachers. Rescue workers recovered at least 90 bodies, with final tolls reported between 90 and 97 dead and more than 150 injured, most of them children. The school's owner was detained over allegations of unauthorized structural additions; the building was found not to have met construction standards.

title: Al-Aaimmah bridge stampede
description: A stampede on the Al-Aaimmah bridge in Baghdad during a Shia pilgrimage killed at least 965 people, mostly women and children crushed or drowned in the Tigris River after rumours of a suicide bomber sparked panic. The stampede followed mortar fire near the Kadhimiya shrine that had already killed pilgrims.

title: Super Typhoon Durian and Mayon mudflows
description: Super Typhoon Durian struck the Bicol region of the Philippines on November 30, 2006, and its torrential rainfall triggered massive mudflows of loose volcanic debris on the slopes of Mayon Volcano, burying villages such as Padang, Busay and Daraga under metres of mud and boulders. At least 1,400 people died in the Philippines, with hundreds more missing, and dozens more were killed when the weakened storm crossed Vietnam; the disaster affected about 3.5 million people and left roughly 120,000 homeless.
sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)

title: Samjhauta Express bombing
description: Two bombs hidden in luggage exploded aboard the Samjhauta Express passenger train near Panipat, Haryana, India, around midnight on February 18, 2007, killing 68 people, mostly Pakistani citizens. The blasts occurred in coaches carrying passengers between India and Pakistan, and a resulting fire intensified the toll.

title: Pasta de Conchos coal mine explosion
description: A methane gas explosion at the Pasta de Conchos coal mine near Sabinas, Coahuila on February 19, 2006 killed 65 miners. Rescue operations were called off weeks later without recovering the bodies of 63 of the dead, and the disaster prompted criticism of mine safety enforcement and workers' rights in Mexico's coal industry.
sources: Mexican Labour and Social Welfare Ministry

title: Niger food crisis
description: Severe drought and a locust infestation triggered a food crisis in Niger affecting 3.6 million people, with UNICEF reporting 32,000 severely malnourished children under five facing death without treatment. A final death toll was never established; UN officials said thousands of children had already died, with overall mortality estimates ranging from several thousand to tens of thousands.

title: Baghdad Ministry Bombings
description: On August 19, 2009, coordinated truck bombings hit the Iraqi Foreign Ministry and Finance Ministry in Baghdad, along with other explosions, killing at least 95 people and wounding about 563 according to Iraqi Interior Ministry officials. The attacks, blamed on al-Qaeda-linked militants and Baathist elements, were the bloodiest day in Baghdad since February 2008 and the worst since US troops withdrew from Iraqi cities at the end of June 2009.

title: Les Issers police academy suicide bombing
description: A suicide bomber rammed an explosives-filled car into a line of young applicants waiting outside a gendarmerie training academy in Les Issers, about 60 km east of Algiers, on 19 August 2008, killing at least 43 people and wounding about 45. The dead included 42 civilians, mostly men aged 18-20 queuing for entrance exams, and one gendarme. It was the deadliest attack in Algeria in years, with al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb suspected, though no group immediately claimed responsibility.

title: Abidjan toxic waste dumping (Probo Koala)
description: Around August 19, 2006, the tanker Probo Koala, chartered by the Dutch commodities firm Trafigura, discharged about 500 tonnes of chemical waste containing sulphur compounds and petroleum slops at roughly 17 open-air sites around Abidjan, Ivory Coast. The dumping caused at least 17 deaths and led an estimated 100,000 people to seek hospital treatment for nausea, respiratory difficulties, skin lesions and other symptoms; the resulting scandal caused the Ivorian government to resign, and a UN investigation found prima facie evidence linking the waste to the deaths and illnesses.

title: Hurricane Katrina
description: Hurricane Katrina made landfall on the US Gulf Coast, breached New Orleans' levee system and flooded about 80% of the city, causing 1,833 confirmed deaths across the affected states. It remains the costliest hurricane in US history, with damage estimated at $81 billion.

title: Cyclone Sidr
description: Cyclone Sidr struck Bangladesh on November 15, 2007, with sustained winds of about 215 km/h and a storm surge exceeding five meters in places. The official death toll was 3,447, with some estimates as high as 15,000; the districts of Barguna and Patuakhali were hardest hit.

title: Hilla suicide car bombing
description: A suicide car bomb exploded beside a queue of police recruits waiting outside a health clinic in Hilla, Iraq, killing 125 people and wounding about 130, many of them civilians shopping in a nearby market. It was the deadliest single attack in Iraq since the 2003 invasion at the time.

title: Battle of Mogadishu (2007)
description: In March-April 2007, Ethiopian and Somali government forces launched a major offensive against Islamist insurgents in Mogadishu, prompting heavy urban fighting that killed approximately 1,200 civilians in the capital. The year as a whole was the deadliest of the insurgency, with estimates of more than 6,000 people killed in Mogadishu in 2007.

title: Red Lake High School shooting
description: A 16-year-old student killed his grandfather and his grandfather's partner, then drove to Red Lake Senior High School on the Red Lake Indian Reservation and killed a security guard, a teacher and five students before killing himself. Ten people died in total, making it the deadliest US school shooting since Columbine.

title: Nias-Simeulue earthquake
description: A magnitude 8.6 earthquake struck off the west coast of Sumatra, Indonesia, causing heavy destruction on Nias Island and killing an estimated 1,300 people, with hundreds killed on Simeulue and the Banyak islands. A small tsunami and widespread building collapses added to the casualties.

title: Amagasaki train derailment
description: A JR West commuter train derailed on a curve and crashed into an apartment building in Amagasaki, Hyogo Prefecture, killing 107 people and injuring more than 550. The train entered the curve at about 116 km/h against a 70 km/h limit, Japan's worst rail accident in decades.

title: Sharm el-Sheikh bombings
description: Three bombs exploded in the Red Sea resort town of Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, including two car bombs that hit the Old Market and a hotel in Naama Bay, killing 88 people and wounding about 200. Most of the dead were Egyptians, and it was Egypt's deadliest terrorist attack at the time.

title: Ahmedabad serial bombings
description: Between 21 and 22 bombs exploded across Ahmedabad, Gujarat, over about 90 minutes on 26 July 2008, hitting 14 locations including markets, buses, and two hospitals where victims of the first blasts were being treated. The attacks killed 56 people and injured about 240-260, according to official government records, and were carried out by the Indian Mujahideen. In 2022 a special court convicted 49 of 78 accused, sentencing 38 to death.

title: Mumbai floods
description: A record 944 mm of rain fell on Mumbai in 24 hours, flooding the city and much of Maharashtra state, halting rail, road and air transport and killing approximately 1,094 people. The flood was among the heaviest in the region's recorded history.

title: Hurricane Stan
description: Hurricane Stan triggered torrential rain and catastrophic mudslides across Guatemala, El Salvador and southern Mexico, burying entire villages including Panabaj near Lake Atitlan, where about 1,400 residents were declared missing and presumed dead. More than 1,600 people were killed across the region, most of them in Guatemala.

title: Kashmir earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck near Muzaffarabad in Pakistani-administered Kashmir, collapsing tens of thousands of poorly built homes and schools and killing an estimated 75,000 people in Pakistan and more than 1,300 in India, with regional estimates reaching 87,000. About 3.5 million people were left homeless.

title: Balochistan earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck the remote Ziarat and Pishin districts of Balochistan Province in southwestern Pakistan on 29 October 2008, flattening mud-brick villages and triggering landslides. The government's final toll was 215 confirmed dead with several hundred injured (official counts rose from 115 to 236 as reports came in), and about 120,000 people were left homeless in freezing mountain conditions. The UN appealed for emergency shelter after an initial government appeal failed to secure funds.

title: Delhi serial bombings
description: Three bombs exploded within half an hour at Paharganj market, on a DTC bus in Govindpuri and at Sarojini Nagar market in New Delhi, killing at least 67 people and injuring more than 200. The blasts occurred days before the Diwali festival.

title: Amman hotel bombings
description: Three suicide bombers attacked the lobbies of the Grand Hyatt, Radisson SAS and Days Inn hotels in Amman, Jordan, killing 60 people and injuring more than 100, including victims at a wedding reception in the Radisson. Al-Qaeda in Iraq claimed responsibility for the attacks.

title: Nevsky Express Bombing
description: On the night of November 27, 2009, a bomb equivalent to roughly 7 kg of TNT derailed the Nevsky Express train traveling from Moscow to St. Petersburg near Bologoye, killing 28 people and injuring about 90. Russian authorities declared the derailment a terrorist attack, blaming militants from the North Caucasus. It was the second bombing on the line, following an explosion in August 2007 that injured dozens.

title: Dongfeng coal mine explosion
description: A coal dust explosion at the Dongfeng coal mine in Qitaihe, Heilongjiang Province, killed 171 miners, making it one of China's deadliest mine disasters of 2005. The blast occurred in a year of repeated major mining accidents in China.

title: Kenya post-election violence
description: After the disputed 27 December 2007 presidential election, in which Mwai Kibaki was declared winner over Raila Odinga, weeks of ethnic and political violence engulfed Kenya in January-February 2008, concentrated in Nairobi, the Rift Valley, Western, and Nyanza provinces. Attacks involved machetes, arson, and police gunfire, killing an estimated 1,100-1,500 people (official inquiries later counted about 1,133-1,220 deaths), displacing some 300,000-600,000 people, and triggering a UN-brokered power-sharing agreement in February 2008.

title: Iraq War (2007)
description: 2007 was the second-deadliest year of the Iraq War. Iraq Body Count documented 26,112 violent civilian deaths during the year, driven by sectarian violence, vehicle bombings, and the U.S. troop surge launched in February 2007. Approximately 900 U.S. service members were also killed, making 2007 the deadliest year for coalition forces.

title: Darfur conflict (ongoing genocide and humanitarian crisis)
description: Armed conflict between government-aligned Janjaweed militias and rebel groups continued across Darfur throughout 2006, marked by attacks on civilians, mass displacement and a severe humanitarian crisis. A September 2006 study published in the journal Science estimated at least 200,000 deaths since the conflict began in 2003, with estimates up to 300,000-400,000 cited by the UN Secretary-General and other organizations, most deaths resulting from violence, disease and starvation. The Darfur Peace Agreement signed in May 2006 failed to end the fighting, and more than two million people remained displaced.

title: Capitol Hill massacre in Seattle
description: A gunman, Kyle Huff, opened fire on a house party in the Capitol Hill neighborhood of Seattle on March 25, 2006, killing six people and wounding several others; a seventh victim died in hospital the next day. Huff then killed himself with a shotgun as police officers arrived, and police later found a rifle in his car and notes indicating he had planned the attack.

title: Tal Afar truck bombings
description: Twin truck bombs exploded in Shia residential neighborhoods of Tal Afar, Iraq, on March 27, 2007, killing 152 people and wounding more than 340. The bombs detonated within minutes of each other, collapsing buildings and burying families.

title: Cyclone Nargis strikes Myanmar
description: Category 4 Cyclone Nargis made landfall over the Ayeyarwady (Irrawaddy) Delta on 2-3 May 2008 with winds of about 215 km/h and a 3.6-meter storm surge, devastating coastal townships including Labutta and Bogale. Myanmar's government reported 84,537 confirmed dead and 53,836 missing, a combined toll of roughly 138,000, with nearly 20,000 injured and an estimated 2.4 million people affected. The Post-Nargis Joint Assessment by the Myanmar government, ASEAN, and the UN confirmed the scale of the catastrophe, which was the deadliest cyclone worldwide since the 1970 Bhola cyclone.

title: Cyclone Aila
description: Cyclone Aila, a severe cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal, made landfall on May 25, 2009, near the Bangladesh-India border, bringing storm surges of up to 6 meters. Final official tallies recorded about 339 deaths across the region, including roughly 190 in Bangladesh and 140 in eastern India's West Bengal state, with hundreds of thousands left homeless and millions affected by flooding and breached embankments.
sources: University of Colorado Natural Hazards Center

title: Typhoon Ketsana (Ondoy)
description: Tropical storm Ketsana (Ondoy) struck the Philippines on September 26, 2009, bringing the heaviest rainfall to Metro Manila in more than four decades — about a month's rain in under 12 hours — and causing catastrophic flash flooding. The consolidated regional death toll reached roughly 900, including 671 in the Philippines, 179 in Vietnam, and dozens more in Cambodia and Laos. Hundreds of thousands were displaced across Southeast Asia.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead) begins
description: Israel launched Operation Cast Lead on 27 December 2008 with air strikes on Hamas targets in the Gaza Strip, including a missile attack on the Gaza City police headquarters that alone killed about 40 people, followed by a ground invasion on 3 January 2009. Over the 22-day offensive, at least 1,387 Palestinians were killed, including roughly 773 civilians and 320 children, with over 5,000 wounded, according to Palestinian and human-rights organizations; 13 Israelis were also killed. A UN investigation found the offensive used disproportionate force and caused widespread destruction of homes, schools, and hospitals.

title: Assassination of Benazir Bhutto
description: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was assassinated at a campaign rally in Rawalpindi on December 27, 2007, when a suicide attacker detonated a bomb after opening fire. At least 24 people were killed, including Bhutto, who died shortly afterward at Rawalpindi General Hospital.

title: Kandahar dog-fighting show suicide bombing
description: A suicide bomber detonated explosives in a crowd of several hundred people watching a dog-fighting competition near Kandahar on 17 February 2008, in an attack believed aimed at a local anti-Taliban auxiliary police commander, Abdul Hakim Jan, who was killed with his guards. The blast killed more than 100 people and wounded about 100 others, making it the deadliest single bombing in Afghanistan since 2001; Kandahar's governor confirmed the toll exceeded 100 as wounded victims died. No group claimed responsibility, though the Taliban denied involvement.

title: Southern Leyte mudslide buries Guinsaugon village
description: A rain-triggered mudslide buried the village of Guinsaugon in Saint Bernard, Southern Leyte province on February 17, 2006, following more than a week of heavy rain. The debris slide, reportedly tens of metres deep, covered the entire village including an elementary school holding about 250 pupils; the official death toll reached 1,126 from a population of about 1,857, with only about 57 survivors recovered.

title: Ulyanovskaya mine disaster
description: A methane and coal dust explosion at the Ulyanovskaya coal mine in the Kemerovo region of Siberia on March 19, 2006 killed 110 of the 203 miners on shift, one of the worst mining disasters in post-Soviet Russia. An official investigation found the mine's methane monitoring and alarm system had been deliberately disabled before the blast.

title: Borujerd (Silakhor) earthquake
description: An earthquake of magnitude 6.1 struck the Silakhor plain region of Lorestan province in western Iran on March 31, 2006, early in the morning, centered near the village of Darb-e Astaneh. The quake killed about 70 people, injured more than 1,200 and damaged or destroyed buildings in roughly 330 villages, with the worst destruction in Borujerd and Dorud.
sources: International Institute of Earthquake Engineering and Seismology (IIEES)

title: Yogyakarta earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck the Yogyakarta region of central Java on May 27, 2006, at shallow depth along the Opak River fault. The quake killed 5,749 people, injured about 38,500 and destroyed or damaged several hundred thousand buildings, displacing an estimated 600,000 residents, and was the deadliest earthquake of 2006.

title: Mumbai train bombings
description: Seven bombs hidden in pressure cookers exploded on crowded Western Line suburban commuter trains in Mumbai during evening rush hour on July 11, 2006. The coordinated attacks killed 209 people and injured more than 700, making them among the deadliest terrorist attacks in India's history; the Indian government blamed the Pakistan-based group Lashkar-e-Taiba.

title: 2006 Lebanon War (33-day conflict)
description: A 33-day war between Israel and the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah began on July 12, 2006 after Hezbollah captured two Israeli soldiers in a cross-border raid. Israeli airstrikes, naval bombardment and ground operations killed about 1,190 people in Lebanon, most of them civilians, according to the Lebanese government and Human Rights Watch, and displaced about one million people; Hezbollah rocket fire killed about 160 people in Israel, mostly soldiers.

title: Typhoon Bilis floods and landslides in China
description: Tropical Storm Bilis made landfall on China's southeastern coast on July 14, 2006, and its torrential rains over six southern provinces triggered severe flash floods, reservoir breaches and mudslides. The final official death toll was 843 people with more than 200 missing, making Bilis China's deadliest storm in a decade; nearly three million people were displaced or evacuated.

title: North Korea floods and food crisis
description: Torrential rains and three major storms in mid-July 2006 caused severe flooding and landslides across North Korea, particularly in South Pyongan, North Hwanghae and Kangwon provinces, destroying about 31,000 houses and inundating tens of thousands of hectares of farmland. Official reports indicated about 600 people dead or missing, while a UN assessment recorded far lower figures and unverified claims reached thousands; the loss of an estimated 100,000 tonnes of food raised fears of famine, and the government rejected most international relief offers.
sources: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)

title: Pangandaran earthquake and tsunami
description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck south of the Indonesian island of Java on July 17, 2006, generating a tsunami that struck more than 300 kilometres of coastline centred on Pangandaran in West Java. The waves killed about 668 people, left nearly 300 missing, injured about 9,000 and destroyed thousands of buildings, fishing boats and tourist facilities along the southern Java coast.

title: Typhoon Saomai strikes China
description: Typhoon Saomai, the strongest typhoon to make landfall on mainland China in 50 years, struck Zhejiang province on August 10, 2006, with maximum sustained winds of about 216 km/h. The storm and its associated rains killed about 460 people in Zhejiang and Fujian provinces, destroyed or damaged hundreds of thousands of houses and coastal dikes, and forced the evacuation of more than a million residents.

title: Malegaon bombings
description: Three bombs exploded on the evening of September 8, 2006 in the town of Malegaon, Maharashtra, targeting Muslims gathered for the Shab-e-Barat festival: the devices were placed near a mosque, in a cemetery and in a busy market. The blasts killed 37 people and injured more than 100; a curfew was imposed and several suspects were later arrested and convicted in connection with the attacks.

title: Maguindanao Massacre
description: On November 23, 2009, a convoy carrying relatives of gubernatorial candidate Esmael Mangudadatu and journalists covering his candidacy filing was stopped by about 100 armed men linked to the ruling Ampatuan clan in Maguindanao province. The 58 people abducted were taken to a hilltop, shot, and buried in shallow graves. Thirty-two of the dead were journalists — the deadliest single event for journalists ever documented by the Committee to Protect Journalists.

title: Sadr City bombings
description: A coordinated attack of multiple car bombs and mortar rounds struck the Shia neighbourhood of Sadr City in Baghdad on November 23, 2006, at the height of Iraq's sectarian civil war. At least 215 people were killed and about 250 wounded, making it one of the deadliest single attacks of the conflict up to that point; the Iraqi government imposed a curfew on Baghdad in response.

title: Virginia Tech shooting
description: On April 16, 2007, a student gunman killed 32 people and wounded 17 in two separate attacks at Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University in Blacksburg, Virginia, before killing himself. It was the deadliest school shooting in U.S. history at the time.

title: Qahtaniya Yazidi community bombings
description: Four suicide truck bombers attacked the Yazidi towns of Qahtaniya and Jazira in Nineveh Province, Iraq, on August 14, 2007, killing 796 people and wounding more than 1,500. The coordinated blasts, which destroyed entire residential blocks, remain the deadliest car bomb attack of the Iraq War.

title: Russo-Georgian War
description: Fighting between Georgian forces and separatists backed by Russian troops erupted on 7 August 2008 and expanded into a five-day war, with Russian air strikes and ground operations reaching Gori, Tbilisi, and other cities, including attacks that killed civilians and a cluster-munition strike on Tbilisi. Georgian authorities reported 412 dead on the Georgian side (about 228 civilians, 170 military personnel, and 14 police), Russian figures listed 64-67 soldiers and about 162-170 civilians killed, with total estimates around 850 dead and roughly 150,000 displaced. Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International concluded total deaths were in the hundreds, not the thousands initially claimed.

title: Baghdad Justice Ministry Bombings
description: On October 25, 2009, two suicide car bombs exploded in quick succession near the Iraqi Ministry of Justice and the Baghdad Provincial Council building, killing at least 155 people and wounding more than 500. Victims included about two dozen children riding a bus near the Justice Ministry daycare. The Islamic State of Iraq, an al-Qaeda-linked group, claimed responsibility. It was Iraq's deadliest attack in more than two years.

title: Mumbai attacks (26/11)
description: Ten gunmen from the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba group, arriving by sea from Karachi, carried out a coordinated 60-hour attack on multiple Mumbai targets beginning 26 November 2008: the Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus railway station, the Taj Mahal Palace and Oberoi-Trident hotels, Nariman House (a Jewish centre), Cama Hospital, and Leopold Cafe. The siege, which ended on 29 November when security forces killed nine of the attackers, left 166 people dead, including six police officers, and over 300 injured; one attacker, Ajmal Kasab, was captured alive.

title: Typhoon Fengshen (Frank) and MV Princess of the Stars sinking
description: Typhoon Fengshen swept across the central Philippines from 20-23 June 2008 with winds up to 175 km/h, causing flooding, landslides, and sea surges. Its deadliest impact came when the passenger ferry MV Princess of the Stars, which had sailed from Manila into the storm, capsized off Sibuyan Island on 21 June, killing roughly 800-850 of the estimated 850-920 people aboard. Including the ferry and flood victims, the Philippine government and UN recorded at least 1,371 deaths in the Philippines and China, with hundreds missing, making it the deadliest Philippine typhoon since 2006.

title: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
description: A dump truck carrying about 1,000 kg of explosives detonated at the security gate of the Marriott Hotel in Islamabad on the evening of 20 September 2008, gutting the building and killing 54 people, including the Czech ambassador to Pakistan, three US citizens, and a Danish intelligence agent, while wounding at least 266. The attack, hours after President Asif Ali Zardari's first address to parliament, was one of the worst terrorist attacks in Pakistan's history; no group claimed responsibility.

title: Karrada double bombing in Baghdad
description: On the evening of 6 March 2008, a roadside bomb exploded in the packed Karrada shopping district of central Baghdad; minutes later, as bystanders and security forces gathered to help the wounded, a suicide bomber detonated a second, larger bomb. Police confirmed 68 people killed and 120 wounded, the deadliest attack in Baghdad in about nine months. Iraqi police and the US military blamed al-Qaeda in Iraq for the double-bombing tactic designed to maximize casualties.

title: China winter storms (2008 Chinese snowstorms)
description: Severe snowstorms, freezing rain, and cold struck 20-21 provinces across central and southern China from mid-January to early February 2008, collapsing power pylons, halting trains and highways during the Lunar New Year travel season, and stranding nearly one million people at Guangzhou's railway station. China's Civil Affairs Ministry confirmed 129 people killed and 4 missing, with 1.66 million people relocated, 485,000 houses collapsed, and economic losses of about 151 billion yuan (roughly US$21 billion). It was China's worst winter weather in half a century.

title: Chinese melamine milk scandal
description: In September 2008 it emerged that infant formula produced by Sanlu Group and other dairies had been adulterated with melamine, an industrial chemical added to watered-down milk to boost apparent protein content, causing kidney stones and acute kidney failure in infants. China's Ministry of Health confirmed at least 6 infant deaths and reported that nearly 300,000 infants had been sickened, over 50,000 hospitalized at the peak. The government withdrew 8,300 tons of tainted products and arrested dozens of executives and officials.

title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead)
description: Israel's military offensive against Hamas in the Gaza Strip ran from December 27, 2008, to a ceasefire on January 18, 2009. Human rights organizations and UN agencies documented approximately 1,340-1,400 Palestinians killed, including around 750-770 civilians and more than 300 children, with over 5,000 wounded. Thirteen Israelis were killed, including 3 civilians. The offensive included heavy air strikes and ground operations and caused extensive destruction of homes, schools, and infrastructure across Gaza.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
Al Mezan Centre for Human Rights

title: Sri Lankan Civil War Final Offensive
description: Between January and May 2009, the Sri Lankan military's final offensive against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) trapped roughly 330,000 civilians in an ever-shrinking 'no fire zone' in the northeast. A UN Secretary-General-appointed panel of experts estimated in 2011 that as many as 40,000 civilians were killed, most by government shelling, with the LTTE also accused of using civilians as human shields. The government's own figures put the toll at about 7,000-9,000. The war ended on May 18, 2009, with the military declaring victory.

title: L'Aquila Earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck the Abruzzo region of central Italy at 3:32 a.m. on April 6, 2009, with its epicenter near the city of L'Aquila. The quake killed 308 people, injured about 1,500, and left roughly 65,000 homeless. Many victims, including 55-66 university students, died in collapsed buildings such as the university dormitory and apartment blocks. It was the deadliest earthquake to hit Italy since the 1980 Irpinia earthquake.

title: Typhoon Parma (Pepeng)
description: Typhoon Parma (Pepeng) made landfall in northern Luzon on October 3, 2009, and lingered over the island for a week, making landfall three times and causing torrential rains. Massive landslides in Benguet province and the Cordillera Administrative Region killed 465 people in the Philippines, with total regional deaths near 500, including in Vietnam and China. Landslide-buried villages in La Trinidad and Baguio City accounted for the heaviest losses.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

title: West Sumatra (Padang) Earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck off the coast of West Sumatra on September 30, 2009, about 45 km northwest of Padang. The Indonesian government confirmed 1,115 deaths, with more than 1,200 seriously injured and about 450,000 people displaced. Widespread collapse of poorly reinforced buildings in Padang and Padang Pariaman district caused most casualties. USGS called it the deadliest earthquake of 2009.

title: Samoa Earthquake and Tsunami
description: A magnitude 8.1 earthquake struck south of the Samoan Islands on September 29, 2009, generating tsunami waves that reached runup heights of up to 17 meters and struck coastal villages with little warning. At least 189 people were killed — 149 in Samoa, 34 in American Samoa, and 9 in Tonga — with many victims children and elderly residents. It was the strongest earthquake of 2009 according to USGS.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

title: Kunduz Fuel Tanker Airstrike
description: On September 4, 2009, NATO aircraft, at the request of German forces, bombed two fuel tankers hijacked by Taliban insurgents near Kunduz City. Villagers had gathered around the stranded tankers to siphon fuel. Death toll estimates range from 56 to 179, with a German parliamentary investigation concluding up to 142 people died, including more than 100 civilians. The strike sparked a major political crisis in Germany and led to compensation payments to victims' families.

title: Peshawar Meena Bazaar Bombing
description: On October 28, 2009, a car bomb exploded in the Meena Bazaar, a women's market in Peshawar, killing approximately 110-120 people — about 70 of them women and children — and injuring more than 200. The blast, among the deadliest attacks in Peshawar's history, destroyed several buildings and trapped many victims in rubble. Pakistani Taliban-linked militants were suspected. The bombing came amid a surge of militant attacks across Pakistan's northwest.

title: Fort Hood Shooting
description: On November 5, 2009, Army psychiatrist Major Nidal Hasan opened fire at the Soldier Readiness Processing Center at Fort Hood, Texas, killing 13 people — 12 soldiers and one civilian — and wounding more than 30. Hasan, a US Army officer, was shot by responding police and survived. It was the deadliest mass shooting on a US military base; Hasan was convicted in 2013 of 13 counts of premeditated murder.

title: Binghamton Immigration Center Shooting
description: On April 3, 2009, gunman Jiverly Wong entered the American Civic Association immigration center in Binghamton, New York, and opened fire on students and staff, killing 13 people and wounding 4 before killing himself. Most victims were immigrants from countries including Vietnam, China, Haiti, and Iraq who had come to the center for English or citizenship classes. It remains the deadliest mass shooting in New York state history.

title: Xinxing Coal Mine Explosion
description: A gas explosion ripped through the state-owned Xinxing Coal Mine in Hegang, Heilongjiang Province, at about 2:30 a.m. on November 21, 2009, while 528 miners were underground. The blast destroyed ventilation and communication systems, killing 108 miners and injuring dozens more. It was China's worst coal mine disaster in nearly two years and prompted the dismissal of mine management and renewed scrutiny of safety in the country's state-run mines.

title: Lame Horse Nightclub Fire
description: A fire tore through the Lame Horse nightclub in Perm, Russia, early on December 5, 2009, during the club's eighth-anniversary party. Sparks from an indoor fireworks display ignited the low willow-twig ceiling, and the fire spread rapidly with lights failing amid panic and a stampede at the exit. The blaze killed 156 people and injured about 100 more, making it one of Russia's deadliest fires in decades and prompting prosecutions of club owners and officials.

title: Mustansiriya University bombing
description: A suicide truck bomb exploded near Mustansiriya University in central Baghdad during the afternoon rush hour on January 16, 2007, killing about 70 people and wounding more than 160. The blast struck a busy commercial street beside the university where students and shoppers had gathered.

title: al-Shorja market bombing
description: A suicide truck bomber detonated a vehicle packed with explosives in the al-Shorja market district of central Baghdad on February 3, 2007, killing at least 135 people and injuring more than 300. The blast destroyed shops and vehicles in one of the city's largest markets on a weekend shopping day.

title: Solomon Islands earthquake and tsunami
description: A magnitude 8.1 earthquake struck near Gizo in the Solomon Islands on April 2, 2007, generating a tsunami that killed 52 people and left dozens missing. Waves several meters high destroyed at least 13 villages across the Western Province.

title: al-Sadriya market bombing
description: A suicide car bomb exploded in a crowded market in the al-Sadriya district of central Baghdad on April 18, 2007, killing about 140 people and injuring more than 150. The blast struck during the evening rush hour, devastating the neighborhood market and surrounding shops.

title: Cyclone Yemyin and Pakistan floods
description: Cyclone Yemyin made landfall on Pakistan's Makran coast on June 26, 2007, bringing torrential rain and flash floods that killed about 730 people in Balochistan, Sindh, and the North-West Frontier Province, with more than 100 killed in Afghanistan. Preceding heavy rain had already caused flooding and hundreds of deaths in Karachi.

title: Peru earthquake
description: A magnitude 8.0 earthquake struck off Peru's central coast on August 15, 2007, killing 595 people and injuring more than 2,000. The city of Pisco was hardest hit, with about 85 percent of its buildings destroyed, and the quake also caused tsunami flooding along the coast.

title: Baghlan bombing
description: A suicide bomber attacked a ceremony at a sugar factory in Baghlan Province, Afghanistan, on November 6, 2007, killing about 79 people, including six members of parliament and a number of children. A crowd of politicians and local officials had gathered for the event.

title: Zasyadko mine explosion
description: A methane explosion in the Zasyadko coal mine in Donetsk, Ukraine, on November 18, 2007, killed 101 miners, making it the worst mining accident in the country's history. An estimated 300 miners were underground at the time of the blast.

title: Algiers bombings
description: Two car bombs exploded about ten minutes apart in Algiers on December 11, 2007, one near the Supreme Constitutional Court and one beside UN offices, killing 41 people, including 17 UN staff members, and injuring about 170. Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb claimed responsibility.
